triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '25. NCU duration is not production latency when profiling replay inflates K1' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 25. NCU duration is not production latency when profiling replay inflates K1

problem.statement: GDN Chunk Forward Pitfalls (CuTeDSL, SM120) -- 25. NCU duration is not production latency when profiling replay inflates K1

payload.attempted: Use NCU `gpu__time_duration` from a metric-heavy bandwidth pass as the wall-clock latency and conclude K1 regressed.
payload.lesson: Use nsys or the strict benchmark for latency. Use NCU for counter breakdown, and label bandwidth as "NCU counter bytes divided by NCU duration."

established_fact.mechanism: NCU can replay or perturb launches to collect requested counters. The duration paired with those counters is valid for counter bandwidth arithmetic, but it is not a low-overhead production-latency measurement.

payload.observed: V122 NCU showed K1 duration `565.09 us`, while the same V113 one-call nsys split showed K1 `383.456 us`. The NCU pass still produced useful memory counters: K1 DRAM `152.45 MB`, DRAM BW `269.78 GB/s`, L2 bytes `1.62 GB`, L2 BW `2.87 TB/s`, and L2 hit `91.32%`.
payload.root_cause: NCU can replay or perturb launches to collect requested counters. The duration paired with those counters is valid for counter bandwidth arithmetic, but it is not a low-overhead production-latency measurement.
